title: HackerTube: YouTube built from videos recommended by HN
summary: HackerTube: YouTube built from videos recommended by HN
detailed: It was Friday night at 11pm, I was tired, I went to YouTube to watch something and realized that I was looking at an enshittified wall of slop.
So this morning (Saturday) I took a hold of my Opus 5.5 and gave it the task: Let's write our own YouTube clone based on whatever videos have been recommended on Hacker News.

Opus downloaded all comments of HackerNews , filtered them, ran Sonnet over them in a Workflow (Claude Code feature), got rid of spam, and narrowed everything down to 40K comments recommending a YouTube video.
In total, we get 6,454 YouTube videos that have been recommended by a few people on HN from 2007-2026 across 150 topics.
sentences: It was Friday night at 11pm, I was tired, I went to YouTube to watch something and realized that I was looking at an enshittified wall of slop.
Insanely exaggerated thumbnails, dumb recommendations of the same tired topics, truly terrible idiocracy-grade content.
I'm sure this algorithm works well for the median person on the internet, but it definitely does not work for me.
So this morning (Saturday) I took a hold of my Opus 5.5 and gave it the task: Let's write our own YouTube clone based on whatever videos have been recommended on Hacker News.
And Opus came back with: hackertube.org !

Opus downloaded all comments of HackerNews , filtered them, ran Sonnet over them in a Workflow (Claude Code feature), got rid of spam, and narrowed everything down to 40K comments recommending a YouTube video.
In total, we get 6,454 YouTube videos that have been recommended by a few people on HN from 2007-2026 across 150 topics.
Then we wrap it up in a YouTube UI, get a domain, push to a VPS, secure, harden, optimize and voila!
EDIT : A little bit more on my process.
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac).
I use Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default.
I don't actually do anything resembling traditional engineering anymore (read/write code, run commands in a terminal, or etc.), I only talk to Claude and have it do everything.

In this case, the only "manual work" I did was: 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box and 3) I bought the domain name.

I worked on this in between Claude's actual work so it still feels a little bit like team work :) Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, deploy, secure, harden and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.
